protocol.name: Compound
protocol.description: Lending markets: Comet (v3) single-borrowable-asset markets and the cToken-era v2 pool.

incidents.note: Absence from DefiLlama’s registry is not proof that nothing happened.

defiscan.summary: Compound-v3 is a lending protocol that accepts a base asset as liquidity and allows borrowing this base asset with a variety of other assets as collateral. Multiple base assets are supported such as USDC, WETH, USDT, wstETH, and USDS. Each base asset represents an isolated lending market managed by a separate instance of the protocol. Compound governance is able to update various parameters for each of these markets.
defiscan.note: DeFiScan reviews each deployment separately. This cell reads 2 reviews: compound-v3/ethereum.md, compound-v2/ethereum.md.

philidor.summary: Philidor scores individual vaults rather than protocols. It rates 5 live Ethereum vault(s) filed under "compound".

risklayer.summary: Compound V2 is a legacy Ethereum lending protocol with roughly $90M in deposits, operating since 2018 under COMP token-holder governance with a 2-day timelock. It has never suffered a direct drain of user collateral, but eight production contracts—including cUSDC—remain unverified on Etherscan, audits are roughly six years stale, and a 4% voting quorum enabled a demonstrated 2024 treasury capture attempt. Overall risk is moderate-high at 5.9/10, reflecting assurance gaps on a deprioritized product whose successor, Compound V3, now receives active development.

details.name: Dependency Risk
details.description: Chainlink reporters with Uniswap V2 TWAP anchor guards limit manipulation; single governance-replaceable oracle path, fixed stablecoin prices, and owner-activated failover concentrate external risk.

details.name: Governance Risk
details.description: 2-day timelock and post-attack proposal guardian partially mitigate, but 4% COMP quorum enabled demonstrated 2024 treasury capture and dual-governor architecture adds complexity.

details.name: Tokenomics Risk
details.description: Fixed 10M COMP supply with no inflation, but top-15 concentration ~44%, depleted DAO treasury, disabled V2 emissions, and mercenary farming history create governance misalignment.

details.name: Audit Coverage Risk
details.description: Nine tier-1 audits through May 2020 and Certora formal verification, but live StdComptrollerG5 lacks post-2020 review and 2021 COMP bug exposed delta-audit gaps.

details.name: Smart Contract Risk
details.description: DAO-governed Timelock admin with ReentrancyGuard and two-step upgrades, offset by 8 unverified contracts (cUSDC, cWBTC2, legacy oracle) and upgradeable Unitroller/cToken delegator pattern.

risklayer.note: Risklayer is in beta and publishes no ordering for its bands, so the figure is shown exactly as reported.

keyFindings.title: cUSDC Market Contract Unverified
keyFindings.description: cUSDC (0x39AA39c021dfbaE8faC545936693aC917d5E7563) holds significant V2 TVL but has no verified source on Etherscan. On-chain admin is the Timelock, yet bytecode cannot be independently audited for delegatecall routing, interest accrual, or liquidation hooks.

keyFindings.title: cWBTC2 Market Contract Unverified
keyFindings.description: cWBTC2 (0xccF4429DB6322D5C611ee964527D42E5d685DD6a) is an active CErc20Delegator with implementation 0x3363bae2fc44da742df13cd3ee94b6bb868ea376 and Timelock admin, but its delegator bytecode is unverified and cannot be source-audited.

keyFindings.title: cAAVE and cMKR Market Contracts Unverified
keyFindings.description: cAAVE (0xe65cdb6479bac1e22340e4e755fae7e509ecd06c) and cMKR (0x95b4eF2869eBD94BEb4eEE400a99824BF5DC325b) are unverified CErc20Delegator instances administered by the Timelock. Users borrowing against these collateral markets rely on bytecode that cannot be reviewed.

keyFindings.title: Legacy Price Oracle (v1) Unverified but Still Referenced
keyFindings.description: PriceOracleProxy (verified) stores v1PriceOracle at 0x02557a5e05defeffd4cae6d83ea3d173b272c904, which is unverified. The proxy falls back to v1 assetPrices() for several underlying assets. Any corruption or misconfiguration in the legacy oracle could affect collateral pricing for markets still routed through the proxy.

keyFindings.title: GovernorBravoDelegate Listed Address Unverified and Stale
keyFindings.description: Discovery lists GovernorBravoDelegate at 0x30065B703DE5d473975A2db5bBB790A23FD6EFbD as unverified. On-chain, GovernorBravoDelegator (0xc0da…) currently points to implementation 0x6f6e4785c97885d26466945055d4ae8931be6f7a. The unverified address cannot be audited and may mislead reviewers about active governance logic.

keyFindings.description: Proposal 62 (Sept 30, 2021) introduced a critical bug in distributeSupplierComp: the condition `supplierIndex == 0 && supplyIndex > compInitialIndex` used `>` instead of `>=`, causing users in cTUSD, cMKR, cSUSHI, cYFI, cAAVE, and cSAI to accrue COMP from index 1e36 instead of zero. ~280,000 COMP (~$80–147M at peak) was over-distributed. keyFindings.title: Single Oracle Path With Governance-Replaceable Comptroller Oracle
keyFindings.description: The Comptroller reads all collateral and borrow prices exclusively from one PriceOracle instance via getUnderlyingPrice(). Admin (Timelock-gated) can atomically swap the entire oracle via _setPriceOracle(), redirecting all market pricing to an arbitrary contract. There is no on-chain secondary oracle or automatic fallback if the active oracle returns stale or malicious prices.

keyFindings.title: Last Third-Party Audit ~6 Years Stale vs Live Deployments
keyFindings.description: The most recent OpenZeppelin audit (COMP distribution, May 2020) predates Governor Bravo migration, multiple Comptroller upgrades (including StdComptrollerG5 at 0xbafe01ff...), and numerous market listings. The September 2021 Proposal 62 Comptroller upgrade introduced a critical COMP over-distribution bug (> operator vs >=) that was not caught by any post-2020 audit.
